 KEY TAKEAWAYS:
 Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif congratulated the national team after its four-wicket victory over India at the Hong Kong Sixes 2026.
 Sharif also praised PCB chairman Mohsin Naqvi and his team for their efforts in supporting the players.
 Cricket fans didn't miss the chance to troll Sharif with sarcastic replies.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Shehbaz Sharif's celebration after Pakistan beat India in Hong Kong Sixes draws mockery
 India and Pakistan have enjoyed one of cricket's fiercest rivalries, but their latest encounter came in a rather different setting at the Hong Kong Sixes 2026 - a niche, six-a-side competition rather than one of the marquee ICC tournaments.
 Pakistan handed India a four-wicket defeat at the Mission Road Ground in Mong Kok. The result was a long way from the teams' usual encounters at the highest level of international cricket.
 However, Pakistan's latest win prompted an enthusiastic response from Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, who took to X to congratulate the team.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement MORE: Can India face Pakistan again at Hong Kong Sixes 2026? Here's why a IND vs PAK rematch is impossible 
 "Congratulations to our boys on a superb four-wicket victory over India in the opening clash of the Hong Kong Sixes 2026! It was a good game of cricket," Sharif wrote on X.
 He also commended Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) chairman Mohsin Naqvi and his team for their efforts in preparing and supporting the players.
 The Prime Minister's decision to hype the result publicly, however, did not go down well with everyone. Cricket fans took the chance to remind Sharif that it was, after all, just the Hong Kong Sixes and not the World Cup.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Cricket fans' sarcastic reactions to Shehbaz Sharif's hype post
 Among the most amusing responses was a parody account mimicking former India cricketer Ajay Jadeja, which sarcastically congratulated Pakistan on what it described as a "Hong Kong Sixes World Cup" victory.
 "Congratulations on winning the Hong Kong Sixes World Cup match against India 😂," the parody account wrote . "Now, it's time for the Victory Parade 😅"
 Journalist Vikrant Gupta was left confused by Sharif's post and simply asked , "Seriously??"
 Meanwhile, a Pakistan fan also mocked Sharif and urged him to stop embarrassing his country. 
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Stop embarrassing us ffs 😭😭🤡🤡," the Lahori Guy wrote, before adding , "Pak got humiliated in last 5 yrs in every icc match Vs Ind and you are celebrating HK Sixes Win that has no value fgs stop being so dumb 🙏"
 India, after all, boasts a dominant record against Pakistan at the two major men's World Cups. They have won all eight meetings between the sides at the ODI World Cup, while holding an 8-1 lead in the T20 World Cup, with Pakistan's only victory coming in 2021.
 Sports journalist Gaurav Kalra also weighed in with a joke, comparing the reaction to the time when Neeraj Chopra won silver behind Pakistan's Arshad Nadeem at the Paris 2024 Olympics.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Huge.As big as Arshad winning the Olympic Gold over Neeraj. Maybe bigger. Sometimes it feels like we are all living in a simulation," Kalra posted .
 Another journalist, Bharath Ramaraj, questioned the Prime Minister's involvement in celebrating the result, writing , "A Prime Minister talking about Hong Kong Sixers. 😂 😂 🙏"
 One fan who is also a CSK supporter, Srini Maama,  wrote , "What absolutely clownery is this! 😂😂😂😂😂😂😂😂😂😂"
 And finally, to cap it all off, one fan jokingly confirmed that the Pakistan PM was actually serious, writing , "No this is not a parody account 🤣😂"

 Can India still progress to the Hong Kong Sixes semi-finals?
 To qualify for the Hong Kong Sixes cup semi-finals, India needs to finish first in the group.
 India have one group-stage match remaining against the United Arab Emirates on Saturday, October 31.
 The UAE have already beaten Pakistan by one wicket, while Pakistan recovered from that defeat to beat India by four wickets. Consequently, all three teams remain in contention for different finishing positions in Group C.

 If India bat first against UAE: India needs to score 104/116/128/140 and restrict UAE to 30/40/50/60 runs, respectively.
 If India is chasing: Chase 31/41/51/61/71/81 within 1.2/1.3/1.4/1.5/1.5 overs, respectively. (not ideal)

 India must bat first against UAE. Note that, even if India beats UAE, they could finish third due to a horrible NRR of of -9.072.
 To state the obvious, a defeat would leave India in third place, sending them into the Bowl semi-finals.
 India's match against the UAE is scheduled to begin at 10:35 a.m. HKT (local time) or 8:05 a.m. IST on Saturday at the Mission Road Ground in Mong Kok.
